title: 2026-11-17_Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_846
description: Security monitoring has detected unusual activity on the target system, potentially indicating the presence of the Sofacy Fysbis backdoor. Your task is to investigate the compromised host, identify the malicious components, and take appropriate defensive actions.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected unusual activity on the target system, potentially indicating the presence of the Sofacy Fysbis backdoor. Your task is to investigate the compromised host, identify the malicious components, and take appropriate defensive actions.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution:
1. List all services:
```bash
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```
This command will display all services, including inactive ones.

2. Filter for active services:
```bash
systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running
```
Look for any unfamiliar or suspicious service names.

3. Inspect the suspicious service:
```bash
systemctl cat systemkernelservicedefender.service
```
This will show the service configuration file, which includes the ExecStart command.

4. Identify the service name:
The service name is `systemkernelservicedefender.service`.

hints.content: Use `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services, including inactive ones.

hints.content: Filter for active services using `systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running`.

hints.title: Third hint title

levels.title: Determine Network Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Inspect the suspicious service:
```bash
systemctl cat systemkernelservicedefender.service
```
This will show the service configuration file, which includes the ExecStart command.

2. Identify the port number:
The ExecStart command in the service configuration file specifies the port number as an argument. For example:
```bash
ExecStart=/bin/sh -c '/usr/bin/ncat -lk 80 -c "cat /var/log/local-inventory/inventory.log" >> /var/log/lab-checkin.log 2>&1'
```
The port number is `80`.

levels.title: Identify System Information Collection Service
levels.content: System information appears to be collected automatically without an authorized administrative purpose. Investigate the host and identify the service responsible for this activity.
levels.solution:
1. List all timers:
```bash
systemctl list-timers --all
```
This command will display all timers, including inactive ones.

2. Filter for active timers:
```bash
systemctl list-timers --state=active
```
Look for any unfamiliar or suspicious timer names.

3. Inspect the suspicious timer:
```bash
systemctl cat local-inventory.timer
```
This will show the timer configuration file, which includes the Unit specification.

4. Identify the service name:
The Unit specification in the timer configuration file points to the service responsible for the activity. For example:
```bash
Unit=local-inventory.service
```
The service name is `local-inventory.service`.
